title: Mexico Recovers 1,132 Pre-Hispanic Archaeological Artifacts Returned from the US
author: La Redacción
content:
_This article originally appeared in the[August 17, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/17/cultura/mexico-
recupera-mil-132-bienes-arqueologicos-prehispanicos-restituidos-desde-eu),
Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. The Consulate General of Mexico in Boston, Massachusetts,
United States, received the voluntary restitution of 1,132 archaeological
objects belonging to Mexico's cultural heritage, the National Institute of
Anthropology and History (INAH) reported. The handover represents one of the
largest archaeological sets received by that consular representation in recent
years and constitutes an example of academic, ethical, and professional
cooperation and of cultural diplomacy for the protection of heritage.

![The restituted archaeological objects](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/artifacts-02-restitution.jpg)Mexico received the
restitution of 1,132 archaeological objects. Photo: INAH

### Collection Includes More Than a Thousand Pre-Hispanic Ceramic Fragments

![Objects from the collection](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/artifacts-03-southeast.jpg)The collection comes from
southeastern Mexico, the INAH determined. Photo: INAH

According to the assessment prepared by INAH specialists, the collection is
made up of pre-Hispanic goods. Notable are 1,053 smoothed, modeled, painted,
and incised ceramic sherds, mainly for domestic use; two complete spindle
whorls; 18 figurine fragments; nine obsidian flakes and 11 of flint, as well
as three stone polishers. It was concluded that the set of objects, which
includes 36 shark teeth associated with the artifacts and potsherds, comes
from southeastern Mexico.

The temporality of the elements is diverse, so the documentation delivered to
the consulate by Jeremy Pilver, a teacher and archaeologist at Farmington High
School, regarding their provenance, will be used to establish datings and
obtain other data useful for research.

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/mexico-recupera-
mil-132-bienes-arqueologicos-prehispanicos-restituidos-desde-
eu_e5163db1-92a2-4bab-a968-435499fba0de_media-1024x632.webp)INAH

### More Than 40 Students Took Part in the Restitution Over Two Years

For nearly two years, more than 40 high school students participated in the
classification, surface cleaning, cataloging, preparation of an inventory and
a digital database, photographic record, documentation, and professional
packing of the collection for its restitution.

The process was coordinated by the Consulate General of Mexico in Boston, in
close collaboration with the INAH and the Secretariat of Foreign Relations
(SRE), as well as with academic institutions of the New England region.
